evidence: E1 (★★): AgentInstruct categorization critique (Q9) — learner identified that 'agentic' is polysemous in chapter §1: (a) agentic *model* (trained model takes env actions) vs (b) agentic *generation pipeline* (multi-agent data synthesis). AgentInstruct only fits (b), not (a). Derived 2×2 matrix (generation × model) and showed AgentInstruct is the *only* paper in §1 occupying the (agentic generation, non-agentic model) cell — odd one out. Concluded chapter author's curatorial decision is 'sloppy' and AgentInstruct fits ch-21/22 better. This is a *chapter-level* categorization critique, not a paper-internal critique — operating at meta-organizational level.

E2 (★★): Teacher-ceiling critique (Q11) — learner observed that SWE-Gym RS-SFT is 'just pass@k = filtered distillation = teacher distribution imitation', therefore teacher-bounded. Extended [[Q5]] democracy framework (which was self-bounded echo chamber) into a *verifier hierarchy*: self < teacher < world. Mapped chapter §1→§2→§3 evolution onto this hierarchy and identified SWE-RL (§3) as the *empirical answer* to the teacher-bound limitation. This connects three separate chapter sections through a single derived framework. Critique directly motivates why §3 exists in the chapter.

E3 (★): Democracy analogy for AutoAct self-consistency (Q5) — learner mapped AutoAct's self-consistency filter to political-science democracy. Critically, the mapping extended past surface-level into *working conditions*: voter independence, diverse information sources, opposition, constitution. Showed AutoAct lacks all of these → groupthink → echo chamber. Connected to subsequent self-improvement literature as 'fixes to the democracy' — RLAIF/Constitutional AI/Kimi-K2 each add a missing element (critic / constitution / external observer). Political-science analogue explains *why* AutoAct saturates better than the paper's own explanation.

E4 (★): RL group-relative learning mechanism critique (Q14) — learner asked 'similarity를 어떻게 학습 신호로 쓰나? 나쁜 시그널 포함 아닌가?'. This is the *exact* question that motivates GRPO's relative reward design over absolute reward. Engaging with the question led to derivation of: (a) GRPO uses group-relative not absolute, (b) continuous reward provides dense information vs binary sparse, (c) KL + format filter prevent worst case, (d) iterative refinement self-corrects single-step noise. Framework move: '*bad signal inclusion is feature not bug*' — counterintuitive mechanism-level understanding of RL with continuous proxy reward.

E5 (★): Cross-group reward variance critique (Q15) — learner extended Q14 by asking about difficulty + patch size dependence in similarity reward. Identified that GRPO within-group normalization handles intra-prompt fairness but cross-prompt gradient magnitude varies with difficulty. SWE-RL paper does not do difficulty-stratified normalization — open problem. Extended [[Q15]] per-objective anchor density framework to *per-difficulty* axis. Extended [[Q4]] distribution overfit to *reward design distribution overfit*. Identified [[Q14]] within-group boundary as cross-group limitation. Three frameworks composed in one critique.

E6: Bootstrap terminology clarification (Q12) — resolved ch-22 verdict deferred item ('bootstrap terminology fuzzy'). Derived 3 ML usages (self-bootstrap A, bootstrap-path B, cold-start C) plus statistical bootstrap distinction. Mapped each ch-27 usage to correct sense. Deferred-clarification-resolution pattern — surfaces parked items at correct future chapter.
